details.label: Discussion
details.text: A cell which formed earlier over the Black Hills in western SD has recently intensified into a supercell while approaching Rapid City. The 00Z UNR sounding showed relatively modest instability (MUCAPE less than 1000 J/kg) and mid-level lapse rates, but strong deep-layer shear around 50 kt. This ongoing supercell should continue to pose a threat for severe hail in the short term per recent MRMS MESH estimates. But, it remains unclear whether it will be able to persist downstream of the higher terrain of the Black Hills given increasing MLCIN with nocturnal cooling occurring across southwest SD. Some short term guidance suggests a small cluster may evolve over the next couple of hours, with some increase in severe/damaging outflow winds possible if this occurs. Regardless, the presence of weak instability and overall isolated nature of the severe threat suggest that watch issuance is unlikely

details.label: Summary
details.text: Thunderstorms should increase through the evening and early overnight hours, accompanied by a risk of severe hail and perhaps a few severe gusts. If convective trends continue to indicate an increase in storm coverage, a WW issuance may be needed

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Isolated thunderstorms are attempting to develop ahead of a surface low, at the terminus region of a geostrophic low-level flow regime. Here, 850 mb frontogenesis/convergence and warm-air advection are maximized, likely resulting the intensifying storms. Though the 00Z mesoanalysis depicts appreciable MLCINH over northeast KS into western MO, isentropic lift should support the increase in elevated convection above the inhibition layer, where storms may take advantage of available instability (e.g. 7.5-9 C/km mid-level lapse rates per 00Z regional observed soundings). 3000 J/kg MLCAPE amid 50 kts of effective bulk shear will support a mix of multicells and supercells tonight, with severe hail and wind the main threats. An instance or two of 2+ inch hail cannot be ruled out. A WW issuance may be needed pending favorable trends in greater storm coverage
